examples.name: Sample — a court scan inside a faxed page (constructed excerpt)
paragraphs: This boundary-only excerpt follows ParseBench-2's text_ocr__contrast page. The outer fax line prints PAGE 04/29. The embedded court scan prints Page 3 of 28 three times: at its upper right, below its court heading, and at its lower right. The outer page ends with the printed filename court document 2.tiff. The personal case narrative and identifying fields are omitted from this teaching excerpt; omission comments below are editorial and are not printed source content.

The stamp below the court heading stays at that printed position; it is not moved to the outer page's header. No additional standalone 3 is supplied. The filename is visible text, not merely an image destination: an image link to court_document_2.tiff does not transcribe it.

examples.name: Counter-sample — treating the embedded page as ignorable content (constructed excerpt)
paragraphs: For the same page, this excerpt loses the court scan and is invalid:

The correct boundary-only excerpt retains the inner document. A complete transcription must also retain the case content omitted for this teaching example. The presence of <sub_page> never authorizes dropping that content. Ordinary columns, tables and text boxes are not embedded pages merely because a border surrounds them.

examples.name: Sample — a statute page as an exhibit
paragraphs: A blue e-filing header in four parts, a red EXHIBIT D label, then a reduced statute page with its own running head H. R. 2617—507, and a red Page 3 of 3 at the foot. Expected boxes: four Page-header elements for the e-filing line, Text for EXHIBIT D, a Page-header for the embedded running head, one Text per statute paragraph, and a Page-footer for Page 3 of 3. The colours are decoration and are not carried.

(2) The term "covered household" means a household, as such term is defined in section 101 of title 38, United States Code, that has a member with a service-connected disability that results in the inability to procreate without medical assistance.
